actualResults: Fresh empty database install, administrator browser creation of two systems and two module groups, published customer/order modules and a secondary workspace passed on dev3.

Ordinary member login and authorized system entry, two-module CRUD, desktop and 390px mobile record views, mobile create/edit, group navigation, title search with matching and empty results, detail, attachment download, PDF printing and one-row CSV export passed.

Assigned and unassigned approval paths, desktop and 390px mobile completion, cross-system application field trimming and denial paths, and primary/secondary tenant isolation passed on the same database.
Administrator browser generated an invitation link; the named account accepted it in the browser and entered the system. One-time invitation token was excluded from persisted evidence.
After publishing MESSAGE:SYSTEM:VIEW to the member role, a fresh session immediately received the permission and viewed three real Flow/export messages on desktop and mobile.
The package contains the Java backend, responsive frontend, database scripts, start/stop/backup/restore scripts and the five named guides. JAR and ZIP hashes match the immutable manifest.

The final package backup produced four hashed artifacts; a new database restore returned 191 tables, Flyway V23, the same five business records and three completed Flow instances, matching attachment bytes, print and export rows.
After stopping and starting the same final package, backend and frontend readiness were UP; attachment, PDF, CSV, cross-system record/Flow and tenant records passed API, MySQL and file readback.

Administrator browser saved and published a new role with MESSAGE:SYSTEM:VIEW, assigned it to the invited member, and read back the effective permission preview. It edited and published customer export configuration version 2.

Administrator browser edited and published approval Flow version 2, republished the public manual approval binding to v2 while retaining the disabled old binding, and published a customer row action. The runtime action required confirmation and changed the selected record status to 已联系.

Administrator browser previewed a two-row customer CSV with one invalid title and zero pre-execution writes, then executed the valid row only; the batch retained the invalid-row error and the audit page retrieved its event and detail.

Personal file center browser upload passed CLEAN scan and protected download returned identical bytes. Operations page rechecked five live dependencies, showed READY, Flyway V23 and the dev3 runtime artifact; API readback agreed.

Corrected administrator and printing guide navigation was packaged in immutable dev4. Dev4 keeps the exact dev3 JAR and frontend file hashes, passed same-database update from V23 to V23 and browser operations readback on version dev4; package ZIP hash and both guide source/package hashes matched.

On dev4, the platform administrator published a PLATFORM_SYSTEMS data source and a platform public dashboard through the UI. Its current V1 runtime showed a READY metric of two accessible systems and matched the platform runtime API.

On dev4, the system administrator published a MODULE_RECORDS customer source and system public dashboard through the UI; its V1 runtime showed three current candidate customer records and matched the system API.

A dev4 platform application internal call exposed that platform login sessions have no memberId while source validation required one, producing APPLICATION_SOURCE_IDENTITY_INACTIVE despite an ACTIVE platform member. Dev5 resolves the member by platform/account; ApplicationScopeHttpTest passed two tests including authorized internal call and ungranted-action denial.

Dev5 same-database update retained V23. Platform application UI publication and an internal CREATE_DRAFT call created a platform-scoped Flow draft; ungranted PUBLISH returned 403. Platform/system dashboard runtime and five live operations dependencies passed browser/API readback after the update.

Dev5 created four hashed backup artifacts and restored them to a new isolated database: Flyway V23, 191 tables, six records, two dashboards, two applications, three Flow definitions and eleven application calls matched source counts. The fixed package restarted; backend 9999 and frontend returned HTTP 200, and both dashboards plus operations health passed browser/API readback again.

After the restore checkpoint, protected personal-file download returned original bytes for its owner, 401 without login and non-disclosing 404 from another system. The import results page safely rolled back the one valid CSV row while retaining the invalid-row error; customer list and system dashboard metric both changed from 3 to 2.

A platform application credential rotated in the UI; the external HMAC request created platform Flow draft #4, an ungranted action returned 403 and an invalid signature returned 401. The one-time secret was not written to durable evidence.

On dev5, the administrator removed the original invited member's sole published message role through the page. Permission preview changed from allowed at version 12 to denied at version 13; page restoration returned allowed at version 14. That account's test password was unavailable, so its attempted login contributes no runtime credit; a new invited account subsequently completed the fresh-login runtime cycle.

The platform application's credential was rotated twice through the UI. A correctly signed ungranted call returned 403 before the second rotation, the old credential returned 401 APPLICATION_CREDENTIAL_INACTIVE afterward, and the replacement credential again reached 403 grant evaluation. Neither call wrote business data.

The existing target system application was configured and published through its page as V3 with both INTERNAL and EXTERNAL channels on the three existing grants. A signed external LIST and DETAIL returned target record #4 and only its granted public_note field; UPDATE and target-scope expansion returned 403 and a bad signature returned 401. A source-system internal LIST still returned record #4. After restarting the dev5 package, readiness and both internal/external calls passed again on V3.

On 2026-10-17 dev5, a newly registered account was invited through the administrator page with the published message role, accepted and entered system #1. Three separate member logins observed message API 200, then 403 after administrator page revocation, then 200 after restoration; the inbox appeared only while authorized. The generated password remained in process memory and was excluded from evidence.

A separate new account saw system #1 in the platform requestable directory but had no accessible systems; direct entry returned 403. Its page request became PENDING, system information page approval assigned the published message role, and fresh login entered system #1 with message API 200. Two requests left by interrupted test attempts were rejected through the administrator page with required reasons and read back as REJECTED.

The target system application was rolled back from its published dual-channel snapshot through the system administrator page. A signed external LIST changed from 200 to 403 APPLICATION_ACCESS_CHANNEL_DENIED while an internal LIST stayed 200. Restoring the dual-channel snapshot through the page published another immutable version, and both calls again returned target record #4. An interrupted first attempt restored the original grant through the API cleanup branch before the completed replay.

Dev5 page inspection confirmed platform organization, role authorization, dictionary and audit entries were generic key/value editors. Dev7 replaces platform audit with scoped event query and detail. V24 repaired 227 unscoped historic platform events in the one-platform candidate database; after new browser checks 236 platform events had platform ID and none remained unscoped. Platform event filter and detail passed, system event detail returned 404, and system-context and unprivileged calls returned 403. System audit UI and internal system application LIST still passed on dev7. The first dev6 V24 script referenced a nonexistent table and failed without changing audit events; the failed Flyway row was removed after inspection, the SQL corrected, and dev7 deployed from the prior four-artifact backup.

Dev9 replaced the platform organization key/value editor with department creation/rename and member assignment. Browser checks covered optimistic conflict, missing department, wrong context and unprivileged denial; database readback retained member roles and scoped audit. Dev10 replaced the platform role editor with role creation, action grant publication and member role assignment. A fresh member gained two platform read actions but could not mutate roles or enter the test system. Revoking organization read made its next request return 403 while role view remained 200; invalid wildcard, built-in role mutation and stale version were rejected. Dev10 immutable ZIP and JAR hashes matched the manifest, same-database deployment passed with the existing MySQL/Redis and a new four-artifact backup. Dev10 scoped platform audit page and internal target-system application LIST also passed; page inspection confirmed the remaining platform dictionary generic editor.

Dev11 corrected the platform configuration route to authorize each category independently. Vue type build and 7/7 permission tests passed. A fresh role-only member opened the real role page; its organization navigation was absent and direct organization URL was rejected. Dev11 keeps the dev10 JAR and V24 database and deployed successfully as one Java backend on 9999 plus one Node frontend.
resolvedReleaseBlockers: Permission Redis cache keys previously collided when isolated databases reused system/tenant/member IDs. Database-scoped v2 keys removed cross-database authorization reuse.
Background job queue, status, attempt and lock keys previously collided when isolated databases reused job IDs. Database-scoped v2 keys let a previously queued export recover and complete.
